subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: Should Telegram local Bot API migration be repaired by endpoint-aware persisted offsets, runtime reset, doctor-only migration, or documentation, and should `400: Logged out` during migration be tolerated at polling startup?
rationale: The source-backed bug is clear enough to keep open, but the fix changes persisted polling state and startup failure semantics, so automation should not choose the compatibility policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Endpoint-Aware Runtime Repair
options.body: Scope or reset update offsets when `apiRoot` changes and add a narrow, tested `400: Logged out` startup tolerance with live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Doctor Or Docs Recovery
options.body: Keep runtime offset semantics unchanged and make `openclaw doctor --fix` or docs own endpoint-switch recovery, accepting that operators must run recovery before polling works.

options.title: Offset Fix Only
options.body: Repair endpoint-switch offsets but keep all Bot API 400 responses fatal, accepting the restart failure during Telegram logOut cooldown.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-Aware Runtime Repair
recommendation.body: Scope or reset update offsets when `apiRoot` changes and add a narrow, tested `400: Logged out` startup tolerance with live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Avant authored the isolated polling ingress path where persisted offsets are handed to the custom-api-root worker, making him the strongest routing candidate for the startup/runtime policy choice.
